Pull request #1203: fix: build linux gnu binaries against glibc 2.17

Fixes the raised glibc requirement of the published linux gnu binaries (#796).

## Root cause

The glibc floor of the shipped binaries was raised twice by CI runner upgrades:

- `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`: ubuntu-20.04 → ubuntu-22.04 (#979) raised it from glibc 2.31 to 2.35
- `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`: buildjet ubuntu-22.04 → `ubuntu-24.04-arm` raised it to glibc 2.39 — the `GLIBC_2.39' not found` error reported on AWS CodeBuild (Graviton)

## Fix

Build the two gnu release binaries with [cargo-zigbuild](https://github.com/rust-cross/cargo-zigbuild) targeting glibc **2.17** (Rust's own minimum for these targets, CentOS 7+), which makes the runner's glibc irrelevant. This covers every report in #796, including CentOS 8 (2.28) and Amazon Linux 2 (2.26). cross wasn't an option here because its aarch64 image is Ubuntu 20.04-based (glibc 2.31 — still too new).

Details:

- The zigbuild release step is ordered **after** the release tests because `cargo test --release` on tag builds rebuilds `target/<target>/release/dprint` natively, which would otherwise silently overwrite the zigbuild artifact with a runner-glibc binary before zipping.
- A guard step runs `objdump -T` on the built binary and fails if it requires any `GLIBC_` symbol newer than the targeted version, so this can't silently regress again.
- The debug builds for these targets also use zigbuild so PRs exercise the toolchain and the glibc check (release builds only run on tags). Tests still build and run natively.
- If glibc 2.17 turns out to be problematic for some dependency, bumping `zigbuildGlibc` to `"2.26"` would still fix every report in the issue.
